saints.name: Saint Andrew Rublev

summary.text: Saint Andrew Rublev was a Russian monk and iconographer, remembered especially for the Trinity icon and for work in Moscow, Vladimir, and the Trinity Monastery.

blocks.text: The OCA places his birth near Moscow between 1360 and 1370. Its life connects his early formation with the Trinity Monastery. He later moved to the Andronikov Monastery, where he became a monk.

blocks.text: Chronicles first name him in 1405 among painters decorating Moscow’s Annunciation Cathedral. In 1408 he worked with another monk on Vladimir’s Dormition Cathedral. He also helped adorn the rebuilt church of the Trinity Monastery after its destruction by the Tatars.

blocks.text: The cited life dates Saint Andrew’s death between 1427 and 1430 and places his burial at the Andronikov Monastery. It records a monk’s repose rather than martyrdom; an exact death date is not established here.

blocks.text: His best-known icon is the Trinity, based on the Hospitality of Abraham. His principal legacy in this account is iconography: images created within the worship and monastic life of the Church, rather than a body of theological prose.
